metadata.notes: Added 2026-08-16, closing a real, previously-missing step: crispy-french-fries.json and salted-fried-potatoes.json both went straight from FRY to SALT with nothing removing the clinging surface oil in between — real technique always drains fried food before seasoning (salt doesn't adhere well to an oily surface, and excess oil is unappetizing left on). REMOVE's own removalMethod parameter (data/actions/remove.json) already names 'poured_out'/'strainer_drain' as real draining techniques, but REMOVE only fires against an instance currently tracked inside a PLACE (recipe-runner.ts's placeContents) — most recipes in this vocabulary, including both forcing cases here, don't use the FILL/PLACE_IN/HEAT_PLACE machinery at all, so a PLACE-dependent verb would be unreachable for them. DRAIN is deliberately standalone, like REST — works on any isDrainable instance regardless of whether a place is involved. DELIBERATELY LIQUID-AGNOSTIC, not oil-specific, even though it was first built for the fried-food case — draining is physically the identical act (removing clinging residual liquid) whether the liquid is oil (after FRY) or water (after BOIL/SIMMER) — see mashedPotatoUseCaseNote below for the second real, genuinely different forcing case that confirmed this generalization rather than requiring a second, duplicate verb.
metadata.methodNote: Two genuinely different techniques with a REAL, cited outcome difference, not just presentation preference: 'wire_rack' (elevated over a tray, air circulates on all sides, oil drips away) preserves crispness — draining on flat 'paper_towel' instead traps steam against the food's underside (limited surface area for oil to actually leave, and once the towel saturates the food sits in a shallow pool of its own drained oil), producing a real, commonly-observed soggy-bottom result the wire-rack method avoids. See REFERENCES.md — multiple convergent consumer food-science sources corroborate the STEAM-TRAPPING mechanism; a specific 'X% oil reduction' figure was found during research but not used here, being an isolated, unsourced number from a low-confidence source, not corroborated elsewhere. 'colander_shake' is the bulk, coarser equivalent (a whole batch shaken in a colander/strainer at once) rather than individual-piece technique — informational only, same non-enforcement depth as every other categorical parameter in this vocabulary. Originally documented as oil-only; 'colander_shake' is also the exact real technique for draining a just-boiled potato before mashing (see mashedPotatoUseCaseNote below) — a real, water-draining use this method value already covered without needing a new one.
metadata.mashedPotatoUseCaseNote: Added 2026-08-17, triaged from an externally-supplied '300 Common Sense Cooking Rules' document (moved to olddocs/ after triage, same convention as every other external report this repo has reviewed) — rule #253's real, cited technique: drain boiled potatoes, then let them steam-dry briefly before mashing (surface moisture left on the potato dilutes butter/milk and produces a gluier mash). Proven end-to-end via data/recipes/mashed-potatoes.json (BOIL -> DRAIN(colander_shake) -> REST(brief steam-dry) -> MASH) — the first real recipe in this repo to actually exercise MASH. See REFERENCES.md and rest.json's own updated durationSecondsNote (widened to a 60s floor specifically for this shorter real case) and hazards below (generalized from hot_oil-only to also name the hot-water/steam-scald version of the identical residual-heat risk).
metadata.actionKindNote: Song, Huang, Sun, Tian, Wang & Li, arXiv:2608.04768 (2026, PAPER_NOTES_2608.04768.md, REFERENCES.md): a bounded, discrete act (lift and shake, or set down on a rack/towel) — the same class as PEEL/CUT, not an open-ended do-until process like REST. Real elapsed draining time varies (seconds to a couple of minutes) but the ACT itself is a one-off, not a continuously-monitored threshold.
metadata.retrySafeNote: retrySafe: true — engine.ts guards addsTag against duplicates, so re-running this after an interruption is a silent no-op, not a double effect, the same reasoning INFUSE/REST already document for their own addsTag outputs.

verification.description: No pooling or visible sheen of liquid (oil or water) remains on the surface or underneath the piece

hazards.note: The food is already out of the oil by this point (a real hazard REMOVE/PLACE_IN already declare), but hot oil still clings to and drips from a just-fried piece while transferring it to a rack or towel — a real, lower-severity residual version of the same hazard, not a new one.

Added 2026-08-17 alongside the mashed-potato use case (mashedPotatoUseCaseNote) — the identical residual-heat risk as hot_oil above, just steam/hot water instead of oil: a just-boiled, just-drained potato and the colander/pot it was poured through are both still genuinely hot.
